title: A Photony Interpretation of Electrons
content: Photony Theory proposes that an electron is not an elementary structure unrelated to light but a localized organization of a high-energy classical photon. Its two interlinked elemental chargephoton constituents continue indexing through quasi-static Planck Space, while an additional c-spin redirects the gamma-ray photon’s forward propagation into a toroidal circulation with a localized center of energy. This article develops that interpretation as the electron companion to A Photony Interpretation of Photons. It separates the proposed internal circulation from experimentally established electron rest mass, charge, spin, magnetic moment, transport, and matter-wave behavior. A substantial examination of electron double-slit experiments emphasizes knife-edge diffraction, aperture boundaries, slit thickness, and the distinct roles of single-slit diffraction and coherent two-slit interference. The established intensity relations and the controlled single- and double-slit measurements are treated as quantitative constraints rather than being replaced by an unsupported, purely geometrical explanation. Electron-mediated chain transduction, reduction, atomic excitation, and thermal coupling are integrated into the structural account. The paper identifies which predictions follow from the Photony hypotheses, which remain conditional, and which require a new electron-boundary dynamical law. The resulting formulation connects photon and electron structure while preserving the empirical demands of quantum mechanics and electromagnetism.
